topic.title: 5 money levels: which one are you on?

title: Payday hits. Which money level are you on? 🪜
description:
Which of the five money levels are you on after payday?
Broke, a $1,000 buffer, no card debt, $500 a month invested at an assumed 7% a year, and a pot big enough to pay the bills at an assumed 4% a year: each level computed. Returns are assumptions, not promises; no product named. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Which level are you on right now? Comment

lines.text: Five money levels. Which one are you on?
Lots of people get stuck early. The last level pays the bills for you.
Level one, me. Payday, and by Friday it's gone. Jar's empty again.
Level two: $1,000 put aside. Then the rain comes, and the buffer holds.
Level three: no card debt. Minimums on $3,000 at an assumed 22.8%: $3,909 in interest. Snip.
Level four: $500 a month, invested at an assumed 7%. After 30 years: $613,544.
The twist? Level four doesn't need a big salary. It needs a head start.
Level five: $1,000,000 in the pot. At an assumed 4% a year, it pays $40,000. Bills, paid.
Level five isn't luck. It's level four, left alone long enough.
Me? Still on one. Payday's tomorrow. So, which one are you on?
